04

Active Creative Styles — Testing in October

Five formats tested this month — Emojis, Jackpot, Spotlight, Magazine Cover, and Game Retro.

01

Emojis

Reaction emojis burst over the card hold, timed to the reveal.

Why test itThe emojis mark the reaction before the viewer reads the card. The pull reads as a moment, not a product shot.

PLAY VIDEO

02

Jackpot

A slot machine spins over the hold and lands on the card, with coins and a JACKPOT stamp.

Why test itThe machine and the stamp mark the pull as a win before the viewer reads the card.

PLAY VIDEO

03

Spotlight

Beams and sparkles lock onto the card, with the player name and team under the hold.

Why test itThe light isolates the card from the background. The name under the hold makes the player readable without covering the face.

PLAY VIDEO

04

Magazine Cover

The hold is framed as a cover: TBC masthead, numbered badge, player name, and a barcode at the bottom.

Why test itThe cover treatment makes the pull look like an issue, not a clip. The numbered badge and the name do the hook before the viewer reads the card.

PLAY VIDEO

05

Game Retro

An 8-bit chibi of the player sits over the hold, with a retro game frame around the card.

Why test itThe pixel style marks the pull as a character, not just a card. The face stays readable under the overlay.

PLAY VIDEO

07

Next Month's Creative Strategy — November

October's read: production exceeded target (352 videos vs. the 252/mo goal, +100 Simple). Hype Confetti led both rankings (100.3 avg. eng., 3,116 avg. views on 30 posts). Total views reached 1,919,400 (↑ 28.0%).

✂️

Retire the bottom three

Banner AI (454 avg. views), Money (349), and Fire + emoji (302) generate the least reach of any label this month. No further production on any of the three.

🧪

Industry News stays, formats get a second read

Industry News ran in October and stays in the mix. The new video formats — GTA 6 / Version 1, GTA 6 / Version 2, Money, Viral Sound Effects, and Nuke Animation — get another month to see which ones hold up outside the first test.

➕

Full Volume in November

Simple remains the baseline format for maintaining posting volume. Industry News stays at 3 posts per day, while new formats continue to be tested alongside it. November will be the first full month with this volume of content.

📊

KPIs for November

Hype Confetti holding the lead is the headline target (100.3 avg. eng., 3,116 avg. views). Secondary: Sports keeps the jump (views ↑ 95.6%, engagement ↑ 139.1%), Card Shop/Breaks stabilizes after the −6.0% views dip, and followers continue to grow past 40K.
